:::{#exr-solve-normal-equations}
#### Solving the normal equations

Using @exr-rss-deriv-intercept and @exr-rss-deriv-slope,
solve the normal equations of @exm-normal-equations-slr
for $\intcoef$ and $\coef{x}$,
assuming $S_{xx} > 0$ (@def-centered-sums).
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-solve-normal-equations}

**First normal equation.**
By @exr-rss-deriv-intercept,
setting $\partial \text{RSS} / \partial \intcoef$ to zero
and dividing by $-2n$ gives
$\bar{y} - \intcoef - \coef{x} \bar{x} = 0$, so

$$
\intcoef = \bar{y} - \coef{x} \bar{x}.
$$

**Second normal equation.**
Substitute that intercept into the derivative from @exr-rss-deriv-slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial \text{RSS}}{\partial \coef{x}}
&= -2 \sumin x_i (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i)
&& \text{(derivative with respect to $\coef{x}$)}\\
&= -2 \sumin x_i \paren{(y_i - \bar{y}) - \coef{x} (x_i - \bar{x})}
&& \text{(substitute $\intcoef$)}\\
&= -2 \sumin (x_i - \bar{x}) \paren{(y_i - \bar{y}) - \coef{x} (x_i - \bar{x})}
&& \text{(subtract $\bar{x} \sum_i \paren{(y_i - \bar{y}) - \coef{x} (x_i - \bar{x})} = 0$)}\\
&= -2 \paren{S_{xy} - \coef{x} S_{xx}}
&& \text{(definitions of $S_{xy}$ and $S_{xx}$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The subtracted sum in the third step is zero
because $\sum_i (y_i - \bar{y}) = 0$ and $\sum_i (x_i - \bar{x}) = 0$.
Setting the derivative to zero and dividing by $-2 S_{xx}$,
which is allowed because $S_{xx} > 0$:

$$
\coef{x} = \frac{S_{xy}}{S_{xx}}.
$$

So the normal equations have exactly one solution:
$\coef{x} = S_{xy} / S_{xx}$ and $\intcoef = \bar{y} - \coef{x} \bar{x}$.

:::
